scores.evidence: OIDC short-lived tokens scoped to one service. Images signed with cosign; Kyverno admission accepts only signed, digest-pinned images
scores.rationale: Mechanisms (OIDC, cosign, Kyverno, Argo pull, expand-contract) are used correctly; minor slips like 'tagged with git SHA' alongside digest referencing and no explicit treatment of fork PR secrets.

scores.evidence: Re-platform in waves. The old pipeline is the system of record and fallback until the service cuts over
scores.rationale: Covers migration, deploy, signing, progressive delivery with explicit deferrals, but omits contract testing, flaky tests and caching/build-time strategies.

scores.evidence: Pull (GitOps with Argo CD). CI never holds cluster credentials
scores.rationale: Consistent GitOps/OIDC/admission design with clear ownership; minor loose ends such as Phase 0 deploying prod before enforce-mode admission and the automated PR bump into GitOps repo trust.

scores.evidence: Red-team: a malicious pull request in the pilot repo tries cross-namespace deploy, a static-key push, and applying an unsigned image
scores.rationale: Validation checks are tied to the riskiest decisions, with measurable thresholds labeled ASSUMPTION, early pilot, and ongoing per-wave DORA comparison and alerts.

scores.evidence: Deploy target. I assume Kubernetes on one cloud. If it is VMs or serverless, the push-vs-pull row flips
scores.rationale: Assumptions and unknowns are explicitly labeled, with how they change the design and where they are confirmed.

scores.evidence: Prod deploys stop when the platform is down. An audited break-glass path, owned by on-call, stays available
scores.rationale: Covers compromise, platform outage, rollback, legacy secrets and decommission risk, but fork-PR secrets, flaky tests, duplicate or partial runs and dependency poisoning are thin.

scores.evidence: Rollback is a git revert in the GitOps repo, which Argo then syncs.
scores.rationale: Deploy, rollback, alerts, break-glass and on-call ownership are concrete and sized for 3–5 people; platform self-monitoring and SLO are thin.

scores.evidence: Runner cost/month | UNKNOWN: finance supplies the budget before Phase 3 wave 3
scores.rationale: Runner cost is identified and load-tested with build-vs-buy choice, but no estimate basis, cost controls or people cost.

scores.evidence: R3: a compromise causes harm that can't be undone, across every service
scores.rationale: Decisions have reversibility ratings, revisit triggers, fallbacks, and the point of no return is isolated and guarded by V5.
Hosted CI with deferred extras is well sized, though Argo, Rollouts, Kyverno, cosign and OTel push the component count against the stated limit.

scores.evidence: Tasks, widest rework first: 1. Freeze the artifact contract. 2. Build pipeline template v1
scores.rationale: Ordered phases with dependencies, exit checks and fallbacks; some details like caching and test strategy are left to the team.

checklist.evidence: Dry-run 5 representative services, one per runtime (V1)
disable its old pipeline trigger only after 5 successful new-path deploys
Immutable image, referenced by digest, tagged with git SHA, SBOM attached
OIDC short-lived tokens scoped to one service.
Kyverno admission accepts only signed, digest-pinned images
Argo Rollouts canary (5% → 25% → 100%) with automatic analysis on error rate and latency.
Throwaway preview environments: when more than 30% of pull requests need manual integration testing.
Load test at 1.5× peak builds/hour (UNKNOWN until Phase 0 history)
An audited break-glass path, owned by on-call, stays available

traps.evidence: Re-platform in waves. The old pipeline is the system of record and fallback
OIDC short-lived tokens scoped to one service.
Each service deploys ... Central, versioned reusable templates that each service pins by version
Buy hosted CI (GitHub Actions or GitLab CI) plus self-hosted throwaway runners

note: Strong risk-driven sequencing with pilot, waves, explicit assumptions and reversibility; weaker on test/flaky handling, contract testing, caching and runner cost estimation.
